ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The flowers of flowering mallow are bisexual flowers. On the mainland, only insects have been observed to pollinate it. On a small island far from the mainland, researchers selected an area where flowering mallow was concentrated and conducted continuous observation throughout the entire flowering period. The observations found that 20 species of insects would enter the flowers of flowering mallow, and 3 species of birds would extend their beaks into the flowers. These insects and birds all came into contact with the pistils and stamens (flower visiting), and the frequency of bird flower visits was clearly greater than that of insects; the birds used pollen or nectar as supplementary food. The researchers randomly selected several healthy growing flowering mallow buds and divided them into two groups: one group was kept in a natural state, and one group used sparse nets to block bird flower visits, and the relative pollination rate was counted (as shown in the figure). From this, is the interspecific relationship between birds and flowering mallow most likely protocooperation or mutualism?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The flowers of flowering mallow are bisexual flowers. On the mainland, only insects have been observed to pollinate it. On a small island far from the mainland, researchers selected an area where flowering mallow was concentrated and conducted continuous observation throughout the entire flowering period. The observations found that 20 species of insects would enter the flowers of flowering mallow, and 3 species of birds would extend their beaks into the flowers. These insects and birds all came into contact with the pistils and stamens (flower visiting), and the frequency of bird flower visits was clearly greater than that of insects; the birds used pollen or nectar as supplementary food. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a bar chart. The vertical axis is labeled “relative pollination rate (%)”, and the horizontal axis has two treatments: “natural state” and “blocking birds.” The bar height under natural state is about 100%; after blocking birds, the bar height is still about 50%, indicating that after blocking birds, the pollination rate of flowering mallow decreased significantly, but did not fall to 0. Then reason: The stem states that birds visit flowers and come into contact with pistils and stamens, and that birds use pollen or nectar as supplementary food, so birds can obtain food, and flowering mallow can obtain pollination benefits; there is mutual benefit between the two. But the figure shows that after birds are blocked, flowering mallow still has about half the pollination rate, indicating that flowering mallow does not completely depend on birds for pollination, and insects and others can still complete a certain amount of pollination; the stem also states that birds only use pollen or nectar as supplementary food, and do not necessarily depend on flowering mallow for survival. Mutualism usually emphasizes that both parties are long-term, close, and dependent on each other, while protocooperation means that both parties benefit but are not necessarily mutually dependent. Therefore, the interspecific relationship between birds and flowering mallow is most likely protocooperation.
